summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Harry Blamires, an Anglican theologian, literary critic, and novelist who lived from 1916 to 2017. It notes he headed the English department at King Alfred's College (now University of Winchester) and began writing in the late 1940s under the encouragement of his friend and mentor C. S. Lewis, his former Oxford tutor.
one_line: Harry Blamires was an Anglican theologian, literary critic and novelist who led King Alfred's College's English department and was mentored by C. S. Lewis.
key_facts: Harry Blamires was born on 6 November 1916 and died on 21 November 2017.
Harry Blamires was an Anglican theologian, literary critic, and novelist.
Harry Blamires was once head of the English department at King Alfred's College in Winchester, England.
King Alfred's College is now known as the University of Winchester.
Harry Blamires started writing in the late 1940s.
Harry Blamires began writing at the encouragement of his friend and mentor C. S. Lewis.
C. S. Lewis had been the tutor of Harry Blamires at Oxford University.
Harry Blamires graduated from University College, Oxford University.
